Judgment:
1. The present is a complaint filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954
(herein after referred to as Pfa Act), alleging that the accused persons have violated the provisi
ons of the PFA Act and Rules

. 
2. As per the complaint, on 09.06.2004, the Food Inspector (herein after referred to as FI) FI Shri S.P. Singh and FI Shri Mittrapal under the supervision of Local Health Authority (herein after referred to as LHA)/SDM) Shri V.P. Singh visited the premises of M/s Pandit Trading Co., Shop No.
45/1, Parwana Road, Khureji, Delhi- 51, where accused Ram Kumar @ Ram Chander was found conducting the business of food articles for sale for human consumption, including "Refined Soyabean oil", which was lying in sealed tan.
The FI disclosed his identity and expressed his intention to purchase a sample of "Refined Soyabean oil" from the vendor for analysis.

The sample consisted of 750 gms. of "Refined Soyabean Oil" (ready for sale) taken from a sealed tin of 15 litre,
bearing label declaration.
The sample was taken under DA vs Ram Kumar @ Ram Chander & Ors the supervision/direction of Sh. V.P. Singh, SDM/LHA.

sentences.text: Before taking sample whole contents of the tin was properly mixed by shaking the tin then a hole was made in one corner of tin.
The Food Inspector divided the sample into three equal parts then and there by putting into three clean and dry glass bottles.
Each sample bottle was separately packed, fastened and sealed according to PFA Act & Rules.
The vendor's signatures were obtained on the LHA slip and wrapper of the sample bottles.
Notice was given to accused No. 1 Ram Kumar @ Ram Chander and the price of sample was also given to him vide vendor receipt dated 09-06-2004.
Panchnama too was prepared at the spot.
All the documents prepared by F.l. were signed by accused No. 1 Ram Kumar @ Ram Chander and the other witness Sh. Mittar Pal, FA.

Before starting sample proceedings efforts were made to join public witnesses but none came forward, as such Sh. Mittar Pal, FA was joined as witness.
3. One counter-part of the sample was also sent to Public Analyst, Delhi bearing LHA Code Number 22/LHA/6069 in intact condition and two counter-parts were deposited with the SDM/LHA in intact conditions.
Public Analyst analysed the sample and found the sample to be nonconforming.

The report of Public Analyst is as follows:
"The sample does not conform to standard of Refined Soyabean Oil.
The sample is of Refined Mustard Oil instead of Refined Soyabean Oil."
4. It is the case of the complainant that the accused No. 1 Ram DA vs Ram Kumar @ Ram Chander &

6. It is further stated that the sample food article was manufactured and supplied to M/s Mahadev Overseas by M/s Kundan Edible Products Ltd., Plot No.1, RIICO Industrial Area, Khushkhera,
Bhiwadi, District Alwar, Rajasthan.

M/s Kundan Edible Products Ltd has appointed accused No 5 Sanjeev Rawal as its nominee under PFA Act and Rules and he is incharge of and responsible for day to day conduct of the business of the said firm.
Being a company accused No. 4 M/s Kundan Edible Products Ltd is also liable.
7. Thereafter on completion of investigation, sanction under section 20 of the PFA Act was obtained from the Director PFA.

The complaint was then filed in the Court on 20.04.2005 alleging DA vs Ram Kumar @ Ram Chander & Ors violation of section 2 (ia) (a) & (m) of PFA Rules, which is punishable under Section 16(1)(a) read with Section 7 of the PFA Act, 1954 by the accused.

sentences.text: 8. As the complaint was filed in writing by a public servant, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused was summoned vide order dated 20.04.2005.

Based on the report of the PA notice was framed against the accused for commission of the offence punishable under section 7/16(1)(a) PFA Act being violation of Section 2(ia)(a)&(m) of PFA Act to which accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.

During the trial, vide order dated 13.01.2010, the accused No. 3 Surinder Kumar Bhardwaj was declared proclaimed offender and proceedings against the accused No.2 were abated vide order dated 11.08.2016.
9.

At the trial, the prosecution examined three witness in support of its case i.e. PW-1 FI S.P. Singh,
PW-2 SDM/LHA Sh V.P. Singh and PW-3 FA Mittrapal.
PW-1 and PW-2 were part of the team that had visited the spot for sample proceedings under the supervision of SDM/LHA Sh V.P. Singh.

These witness narrated the steps undertaken by them during the sample proceedings, including disclosing their identity, expressing intention to purchase sample for analysis, lifting the sample of 750 gms of "Refined Soyabean oil" from sealed tin after opening the sealed tin from the vendor for analysis having label identical declaration, dividing the sample into three counterparts by putting into three clean and dry bottles, separately sealing, packing and marking the same and obtaining signatures of vendor and witnesses.
They also DA vs Ram Kumar @ Ram Chander & Ors proved the necessary documents including the vendor's receipt Ex.PW-1/A, Notice Ex.PW-1/B, Panchnama Ex.PW-1/C.

Thereafter, PA Report Ex.PW-1/F was received according to which the sample does not conform to standard.

During investigation, vendor furnished statement Ex.PW1/G stating that he purchased the sealed tin of which the sample was lifted from M/s Mahadev Overseas, East Moti Bagh, Sarai,

PW-1 also sent a letter Ex.PW1/l to M/s Mahadev Overseas and received reply Ex.PW1/l1 alongwith photocopy of Sales Tax Registration and Bill of purchase of 'Kundan Edible Products Ltd'.
Mark-Y. PW-1 also sent a letter Ex. PW1/J to STO Ward No. 41 and as per reply at portion A, Sh Surender Kumar and Govind Sharma were partners of the firm of M/s Mahadev Overseas.
PW-1 also received reply Ex.PW1/K from M/s Kundan Edible Products Ltd alongwith certificate of registration and copy of Form-Vlll in favour of Sh. Sanjeev Rawal as their nominee Ex. PW1/K1.

PW-1 also got confirmed from CMO, Alwar in respect of nomination of 'Kundan Edible Products Ltd' and as per reply Ex. PW1/K2, accused Sanleev Rawal was DA vs Ram Kumar @ Ram Chander & Ors Nominee of the company.

sentences.text: After completion of the investigation, the complete case file along with all the statutory documents were sent to the then Director Sh. Duwab Cgabd through LHA, who after going through the entire case file, applied his mind and gave the sanction for prosecution Ex.PW1/L against the accused person.
Thereafter the present complaint Ex.PW1/M was filed in the Court and then the intimation letter Ex.PW1/N was sent along with the PA report by registered post Ex.PW1/O to accused.
The witnesses were duly cross examined by the Ld Defence counsel.
10. Statement of the accused under section 313 CrPC were recorded on 22.07.2013 wherein the accused denied the allegations and pleaded innocence.
Thereafter the accused did not lead defence and vide order dated 08.10.2013, defence evidence was closed and the matter was fixed for final arguments.
11. In a criminal case, the burden is only on the prosecution to prove its case against the accused beyond reasonable doubt by leading positive evidence.
This burden cannot be shifted to the accused and it has to be necessary discharged by the prosecution itself.
12. In the present case the prosecution alleges that the sample commodity that is soyabean oil purchased from accused no.1 is not as per standard.
The case of the prosecution as reflected from the the complaint as well as the testimony of all the three witnesses is that the commodity purchased from accused no. 1 was refined soyabean oil.

Its not the case of the prosecution that the food inspector took the sample of some other commodity or DA vs Ram Kumar @ Ram Chander & Ors that in the name of soyabean the accused no. 1 was selling mustard oil.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The team which went to purchase had opened the tin from which the sample commodity was purchased.

They while taking the sample of 750 gms of "Refined Soyabean oil" from sealed tin after opening the sealed tin from the vendor for analysis, divided the sample into three counterparts by putting into three clean and dry bottles.
If it would have been mustard oil in place of soyabean oil they could have easily detected it.
Since nothing of that sort happened there it is clear that the sample they purchased was of soyabean oil.
13. But it appears that the sample sent for testing to PA was not the same sample because the PA reported that the sample was of mustard oil.

It seems that there was some mistake on the part of the complainant in sending the right kind of sample to the public analyst due to which the result of Da vs Ram Kumar @ Ram Chander & Ors on 16 April, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4302232/
4 public analyst has not come properly.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In such eventuality the accused are entitled to be acquitted.
14. Therefore on the basis of the aforesaid discussion all the accused including accused No. 3 Surinder Kumar, who is a proclaimed offender are acquitted from the present case.
